function.name: create_a_docker_file
function.description: This function generates a Dockerfile in the specified directory with basic configuration. The Dockerfile will be tailored to a simple Python application. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

directory_name.description: The name of the directory where the Dockerfile will be created. It should be a valid directory path relative to the current working directory.

base_image.description: The base image to use for the Dockerfile, representing the starting point for the build.

maintainer.description: The name of the maintainer or author of the Dockerfile.

expose_port.description: The port number that the container should expose. This is typically the port that the application listens on.

entrypoint.description: The command that will be executed when the Docker container starts.

function.name: create_kubernetes_yaml_file
function.description: Generates a Kubernetes deployment and service YAML file in the specified repository directory. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

directory_name.description: The name of the directory where the Kubernetes YAML file will be created. This should be the root directory of the repository.

deployment_name.description: The name of the deployment to be created. This should be a unique identifier for the deployment.

image_name.description: The name of the Docker image to be used in the deployment. Include the image version tag if necessary.

replicas.description: The number of replicated pods desired in the deployment.

port.description: The port number that the container exposes for communication.

service_type.description: The type of Kubernetes service to be created for the deployment.

message.content:
Below is a complete “starter kit” you can drop into the **nodejs‑welcome** repository.  
It contains:

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `Dockerfile` | Builds a lightweight Node.js image. |
| `k8s/deployment.yaml` | Deployment + Service for Kubernetes. |
| `.github/workflows/ci.yml` | GitHub Actions workflow that builds the app and pushes a Docker image to GHCR on every push to `main`. |

> **NOTE** – The repo you cloned is a Node.js project, so the Dockerfile uses the official Node image.  
> The helper functions you saw only support Python images, so we’re writing the files manually.

---

## 1. Dockerfile

Create a file named `Dockerfile` at the root of the repo:

```dockerfile
# Dockerfile
# ------------------------------------
# Use the official Node.js 14 image (Alpine for small size)
FROM node:14-alpine

# Create app directory
WORKDIR /app

# Copy package files first to leverage Docker cache
COPY package*.json ./

# Install production dependencies
RUN npm install --production

# Copy the rest of the source code
COPY . .

# Expose the port your app listens on
EXPOSE 3000

# Start the application
CMD ["node", "app.js"]
```

> **Why this Dockerfile?**  
> * `node:14-alpine` is small and stable.  
> * Installing dependencies before copying the rest of the code lets Docker cache the layer.  
> * `EXPOSE 3000` matches the default port used by the sample app.  
> * `CMD ["node", "app.js"]` starts the server.

---

## 2. Kubernetes YAML

Create a directory `k8s/` (or any name you prefer) and add `deployment.yaml` inside it:

```yaml
# k8s/deployment.yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: nodejs-welcome-deployment
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: nodejs-welcome
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: nodejs-welcome
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: nodejs-welcome
        image: ghcr.io/${{ github.repository_owner }}/nodejs-welcome:latest
        ports:
        - containerPort: 3000
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: nodejs-welcome-service
spec:
  type: ClusterIP
  selector:
    app: nodejs-welcome
  ports:
  - port: 80
    targetPort: 3000
```

> **What this does**  
> * Deploys two replicas of the app.  
> * Exposes the container port 3000 to the cluster via a `ClusterIP` service on port 80.  
> * The image name uses the GitHub Container Registry (`ghcr.io`) – you’ll push the image there in the CI workflow.

---

## 3. GitHub Actions Workflow

Create the directory `.github/workflows/` (if it doesn’t exist) and add `ci.yml`:

```yaml
# .github/workflows/ci.yml
name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
      # Checkout the repo
      - uses: actions/checkout@v3

      # Set up Node.js
      - name: Set up Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v3
        with:
          node-version: '14'

      # Install dependencies
      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm ci

      # Run tests (optional – adjust if you don’t have tests)
      - name: Run tests
        run: npm test

      # Build Docker image
      - name: Build Docker image
        run: |
          docker build -t ghcr.io/${{ github.repository_owner }}/nodejs-welcome:${{ github.sha }} .
        env:
          DOCKER_BUILDKIT: 1

      # Log in to GitHub Container Registry
      - name: Log in to GHCR
        uses: docker/login-action@v2
        with:
          registry: ghcr.io
          username: ${{ github.actor }}
          password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}

      # Push Docker image
      - name: Push Docker image
        run: |
          docker push ghcr.io/${{ github.repository_owner }}/nodejs-welcome:${{ github.sha }}
```

> **Key points**  
> * Uses the built‑in `GITHUB_TOKEN` secret for authentication.  
> * Builds the image with the commit SHA as the tag (you can change to `latest` if you prefer).  
> * Pushes the image to GHCR so you can deploy it to Kubernetes.

---

## 4. Add, Commit, Push

Open a terminal in the repo root and run:

```bash
# Stage the new files
git add Dockerfile k8s/deployment.yaml .github/workflows/ci.yml

# Commit
git commit -m "Add Dockerfile, Kubernetes manifests, and CI workflow"

# Push to main
git push origin main
```

If you’re on a different branch, replace `main` with your branch name.

---

## 5. Verify

1. **Dockerfile** – Run `docker build -t test .` locally to ensure it builds.  
2. **Kubernetes** – Apply the manifest:  
   ```bash
   kubectl apply -f k8s/deployment.yaml
   ```  
   Check pods: `kubectl get pods -l app=nodejs-welcome`.  
3. **GitHub Actions** – Push a change to `main` and watch the workflow run under *Actions* → *CI*.

That’s it! Your repo now has a working Docker image, Kubernetes deployment, and CI pipeline that automatically builds and pushes the image whenever you push to `main`.
